items.title: Endpoint integration of a backward exponential kernel

source.attribution: Mathlib supplies monotonicity from a nonnegative derivative; Samplinglib packages the exact exponential convolution used in semigroup interpolation.

items.statement: If H starts at zero and its derivative on (0,t) is bounded by a backward exponential kernel, then H(t) is bounded by the exact integrated kernel.
assumptions: The decay rate is strictly positive and t is nonnegative.
H has the supplied derivative H' throughout the closed interval [0,t].
H(0)=0 and H'(s) is bounded above by source·exp(-rate(t-s))·energy on the open interval.
No separate sign condition on source or energy is required.

obligations.label: Integrate the backward exponential derivative bound exactly

bindings.boundary: The theorem integrates a supplied scalar derivative estimate; it does not construct a semigroup or prove an entropy derivative or gradient-contraction identity.

assumption_deltas.source: The fundamental-theorem argument is usually stated under continuous differentiability.
assumption_deltas.lean: Lean asks only for an exact derivative at each point of [0,t] and uses monotonicity of an explicit comparison primitive.
assumption_deltas.reason: The pointwise HasDerivAt hypotheses provide all continuity and differentiability consumed by the proof.
